items.stem: A fruit seller has 100 fruits: 40 apples, 30 bananas, 20 oranges, 10 mangoes. If one fruit is chosen, is the probability of selecting a banana or orange greater than that of selecting an apple?
items.answer: Probability of banana or orange = (30+20)/100 = 50/100. Probability of apple = 40/100. Since 50/100 > 40/100 → Yes, banana/orange > apple.

items.stem: A cinema hall has 300 seats: 120 balcony, 100 middle, 80 front. If one seat is chosen, is the probability of selecting a balcony seat greater than 1/3?
items.answer: P(Balcony) = 120/300 = 2/5 = 0.4. Compare with 1/3 ≈ 0.33. Since 0.4 > 0.33 → Yes, balcony > 1/3.

items.stem: During a shopping festival, 80 coupons were distributed: 30 for clothes, 25 for electronics, 15 for groceries, and 10 for toys. If one coupon is picked at random: (i) Identify which category has the lowest probability of being selected after computation of probability of each category being selected. (ii) Is the probability of selecting a clothes coupon greater than 1/3? Justify
items.answer: Probabilities: P(Clothes) = 30/80 = 3/8, P(Electronics) = 25/80 = 5/16 P(Groceries) = 15/80 = 3/16 P(Toys) = 10/80 = 1/8 (i) Toys have the lowest probability. (ii) Yes, the probability of selecting a clothes coupon is greater than one-third.

items.stem: Compare the probability of getting a prime number and the probability of getting a composite number when a die is thrown
items.answer: P(Prime) = 3/6 = 1/2. P(Composite) = 2/6 = 1/3. Since 1/2 > 1/3 SO Probability of getting Prime > Probability of getting Composite.

items.stem: In a test, 40 students appeared: 10 full marks, 15 above average, 10 below average, 5 failed. Is the probability of selecting a student who did not fail greater than 0.85?
items.answer: P(Not failed) = 35/40 = 0.875. Compare with 0.85. Since 0.875 > 0.85 So, Yes, probability > 0.85. 3 MARKS

items.stem: A cricket team played 12 matches: won 7, lost 4, draw 1. (i) Find the probability of selecting a match they won. (ii) Compare the probability of losing with drawing. (iii) State whether the probability of winning is greater than 1/2.
items.answer: Probability of Winning = 7/12; Probability of getting Losing > Probability of having Draw Probability of Winning > 1/2

items.stem: A die is rolled once.(i) Find the probability of getting a prime number. (ii) Compare the probability of getting a composite number with a prime number. (iii) State whether the probability of getting an odd number is equal to the probability of getting an even number.
items.answer: Probability of getting Prime = 3/6 = 1/2; Probability of getting Composite = 2/6 = 1/3 So, Probability of getting Prime > Probability of getting Composite; P(Odd) = P(Even )= 3/6= 1/2

items.stem: A factory produces 500 toys: 450 good and 50 defective. (i)Find the probability of selecting a defective toy. (ii)Compare the probability of selecting a good toy with a defective toy. (iii)State whether the probability of selecting a good toy is more than 4/5.

In a class of 40 students: 18 study Mathematics, 12 study Science, 10 study both. (i)Find the probability of selecting a student who studies only Mathematics. (ii)Compare the probability of studying Science with studying both subjects. (iii)Justify: the probability of studying Maths is greater than 1/3.
items.answer: Probability of student studying Only Maths = 8/40; Probability of student studying Science = 12/40 > Probability of student studying Both = 10/40; Probability of student studying Maths = 18/40 > 1/3

A hospital has 120 patients: 50 children, 40 adults, and 30 senior citizens. If one patient is chosen at random: (i) Identify which group has the highest probability of being selected (ii) Compare the probability of selecting an adult with that of selecting a senior citizen. (iii) State which group has the highest probability of being selected if one patient is chosen at random.
items.answer: Highest = Children; P(Adults) > P(Seniors); Highest group = Children 5 marks

items.stem: At an airport, 200 passengers are checked: 90 carry handbags, 70 carry backpacks, and 40 carry suitcases. If one passenger is chosen at random, find the probability that the passenger is: (i) carrying a handbag (ii) (ii) carrying a backpack (iii) (iii) carrying a suitcase (iv) (iv) not carrying a suitcase (v) (v) either a handbag or a backpack
items.answer: Probability of Carrying Handbag = 90/200=9/20 Probability of Carrying Backpack = 70/200=7/20 Probability of Carrying Suitcase = 40/200 =1/5 Probability of Not Carrying suitcase = 160/200 = 4/5 P(Handbag + Backpack) = 160/200= 4/5

items.stem: A restaurant served 150 meals in a day: 60 vegetarian, 50 non-vegetarian, and 40 vegan. If one meal order is chosen at random, find the probability that it is: (i) vegetarian (ii) non-vegetarian (iii)vegan (iv)not vegan (v) either vegetarian or vegan.

A bus company issues 100 tickets: 25 window, 35 aisle, and 40 middle seats. If one ticket is chosen at random, find the probability that it is: (i) a window seat (ii) an aisle seat (iii) a middle seat (iv) not a window seat (v) either aisle or middle seat
items.answer: Probability of getting Window seat = 25/100 = ¼ Probability of getting Aisle seat= 35/100 Probability of getting Middle = 40/100= 4/10=2/5 Probability of Not getting window seat = 75/100= ¾ P( Aisle+Middle) = 75/100= 3/4

items.stem: In a shopping mall, 250 customers bought items: 100 bought clothes, 80 bought electronics, 50 bought groceries, and 20 bought books. If one customer is chosen at random, find the probability that the customer bought: (i) clothes (ii) electronics (iii) groceries (iv) not books (v) either clothes or electronics
items.answer: Probability of selecting Clothes = 100/250 = 2/25 Probability of selecting Electronics = 80/250 = 8/25 Probability of selecting Groceries = 50/250 =1/5 Probability of selecting Not books = 230/250 = 23/25 Probability of selecting Clothes+ Electronics = 180/250= 18/25 Case study

items.stem: A school is organizing a picnic for 60 students. Out of them, 25 chose sandwiches, 20 chose fruits, and 15 chose snacks. (i) Find the probability most chosen food item (ii) State whether the probability of choosing fruits is less than 1/3. (iii) If one student is chosen at random, find the probability that the student chose either sandwiches or snacks.
items.answer: P(Sandwiches) = 25/60 = 5/12 Most chosen food item is Sandwiches P(Fruits) = 20/60 < 1/3 P(Sandwiches +Snacks) = 40/60= 2/3

(ii) Is the probability of selecting a car greater than 1/3? (iii) If one vehicle is chosen at random, find the probability that it is either a bike or scooter.

An online store sold 100 items in a day: 40 clothes, 30 electronics, 20 books, and 10 toys. (i) Which category has a probability of exactly 1/5 of being selected? (ii) Is the probability of selecting electronics equal to the probability of selecting books plus toys together? (iii) If one item is chosen at random, find the probability that it is not clothes.
items.answer: Probability is 1/5 = 20/100 The category is books P(Electronics) = 30/100 = 3/10 P(Books +Toys) = 30/100 = 3/10 P(Not clothes) = 60/100 = 3/5
